blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: Hazelmere is a rural community and board sub-area on the southeast side of the City of Surrey — the acreage ground around 16 Avenue and 184 Street running south toward 0 Avenue and the US border, also known locally as Hall's Prairie — and one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock", inside the City's South Surrey community. The Little Campbell River winds through it toward Boundary Bay, and much of its watershed is farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere.

Community context only (whole S Surrey White Rock community, not Hazelmere's prices): Detached median $1,628,000; Condos & Townhomes median $700,000 / $524 per sq ft / 99% sale-to-list / 33 DOM. Per-sub-area medians are not published: Not verified at sub-area level.
This is effectively a car-only sub-area on the sources checked.

Planning frame to the north: the South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan ground sits immediately north of Hazelmere's southern lands; the City's plan document records that Hall's Prairie was renamed Hazelmere after the rail station named for Henry Thrift's homestead, and that Hazelmere largely maintained its rural, agricultural character over the past century.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Hazelmere Guide

items.t: ALR housing frame (governs any Hazelmere parcel in the ALR): land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel; a principal residence may be up to 500 m² total floor area without ALC application; one additional detached residence may be permitted of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha; a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence and only where local bylaws allow it; local governments may further restrict residences through zoning.

SSMUH caution for this ground: Surrey's SSMUH allowances apply to eligible residential-zoned properties under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary, with exemptions including lands not connected to community water and sewer — most Hazelmere acreage ground is outside that shape, so the standard 3–4 unit framing must not be applied to a Hazelmere lot without a parcel check. Where SSMUH does apply, a secondary suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable floor area under Bylaw 12000.

blocks.text: Good to know about Hazelmere Guide

items.t: The watershed has no dykes. The guide page states (site copy compiled from the City of Surrey per the page) that the Little Campbell River watershed covers over 60 km² from the Township of Langley through Surrey to Boundary Bay, is mostly rural residential and agricultural with a large part in the ALR, has no dykes, and its floodplain follows the river channel closely.

Heritage here is stated as guide-page site copy. Hazelmere United Church, 1614 184 Street, built 1903 in Carpenter Gothic style; Hazelmere Cemetery, 19184 16 Avenue, established when the Hall's Prairie Cemetery Co. incorporated in 1908; and the Hall's Prairie South Building at 18035 8 Avenue, built about 1927 — all three on the City's heritage site list per the guide page, attributed there to City of Surrey heritage pages.
Recreation is private, not municipal, on the sources read.
The feed mixes two different products. Price the parcel, not the feed.
Travel time to any hospital: Not verified.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Hazelmere
What trades here

items.t: Lot fabric: Servicing is parcel-specific and varies inside the sub-area: the page's general guidance is private wells and onsite septic for rural homes, yet one feed listing is described in its own text as on city sewer and water — both positions are carried, and neither is generalised to the sub-area. No typical lot size or lot price is stated as a profile.

Fee-simple lots are the default form: an acreage parcel here is fee-simple unless title says otherwise — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. The one built strata complex in the sub-area, Hazelmere Village, is a townhouse complex (cross-reference below), not a lot form. A sub-area-wide strata-versus-freehold split is not verified.

: a bare-land strata lot is strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is not fee-simple. No bare-land strata plan inside Hazelmere was verified — no such plan is named or counted, and tenure on any specific parcel is a title question.

Zoning character, as the page states it (Not verified on the bylaw text): A-1 General Agriculture zoning for Hazelmere Valley acreages, with Part 10 (Bylaw 12000) minimum lot areas of 4 hectares inside the ALR and 2 hectares outside it for new A-1 lots, one single-family dwelling which may contain one secondary suite under A-1, and RA Acreage Residential zoning on some nearby land with a 4,050 m² minimum. The RA figure is consistent with the City's SSMUH zone table (RA lots at over 4,050 m²); the A-1 / Part 10 figures themselves were not re-read in Bylaw 12000 — confirm in the current consolidated bylaw before quoting them for a parcel.
Built stock — cross-reference only, never land

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals, documented as such, never as inventory: none is documented as a named proposal in this sub-area's research. Two framing items are documented AS planning context only: (1) a feed parcel whose listing text frames it as land in a townhouse-designated plan area — a listing framing, not a plan confirmation opened; and (2) the South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan ground immediately north — a City plan area, not a development site and not Hazelmere lot inventory.
ALR vs non-ALR split: Not verified — no ALC map result for a Hazelmere parcel was opened, and no share is stated. Check every parcel on the ALC maps by PID or civic address before pricing it.

items.t: Hazelmere is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock" in the SnapStats data, inside the City of Surrey's South Surrey community — one of the City's seven communities. (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)

Names and history: "Hazelmere" (board, City heritage name and page name) and "Hall's Prairie" (the older local name). The City's South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan document records that Hall's Prairie was renamed Hazelmere after the rail station named for Henry Thrift's homestead, and that Hazelmere largely maintained its rural, agricultural character over the past century. That plan ground — approximately 249 hectares centred around 16 Avenue and 192 Street, immediately south of Campbell Heights Business Park — sits immediately north of Hazelmere's southern lands; the 249-hectare figure is carried from the City's display-boards document via search result and was not located in the full plan text's verification pass, so it is not verified on the plan text here.

Schools (Ministry-listed names and addresses only): Xw'epiteng Elementary, 18035 8 Ave (the school physically in Hazelmere); East Kensington Elementary, 2795 184 St; Douglas Elementary, 17325 2 Ave; Earl Marriott Secondary, 15751 16 Ave (level read from its name — the Ministry level field mislabels it).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Hazelmere

items.t: ALR rules (these govern any Hazelmere parcel that is in the ALR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel — a principal residence up to 500 m² total floor area without ALC application, a secondary suite only inside the principal residence and only where local bylaws allow it, and at most one additional detached residence of up to 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha); local governments may further restrict residences through zoning. Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — not a flat "$2,500+". Whether a specific Hazelmere property has farm class is a question for BC Assessment and that parcel, and is not confirmed here.

Secondary suites / coach houses (urban Surrey frame, for completeness — not assumed to govern A-1 ground): one suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit and never inside a coach house or garden suite; coach/garden suites 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR). On A-1 / ALR parcels the ALR block above and the parcel's zone govern first.

blocks.text: Good to know about Hazelmere

items.t: The highest ratio in the set rests on two sales. A land price case here needs parcel-level comparables, not the ratio and not the $1,628,000 community median.
"Partly in the ALR" is a real parcel condition here, not a hedge.

A serviced lot inside a "well and septic" area is not a contradiction. The feed itself carries a just-under-1-acre property described as on city sewer and water alongside the page's rural well/septic guidance — servicing follows the parcel's street and connections, not the sub-area's reputation.

The old name explains the ground. Hall's Prairie became Hazelmere after Henry Thrift's homestead rail station, and the City's plan document says the district kept its rural, agricultural character for a century — the acreage fabric is the historic fabric, not leftover urban lots.

A townhouse-designation framing in a listing is not a plan document. One feed parcel is described in its own listing text as land in a townhouse-designated plan area; no plan confirmation was found for that parcel, so the designation is not verified and the parcel is priced only after a COSMOS / plan check.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Hazelmere
What a duplex looks like in Hazelmere

items.t: Farm-residence form — stated only as ALR sources support: Where a Hazelmere parcel is in the ALR, the ALC frame is one principal residence up to 500 m², a secondary suite only inside that residence and only where local bylaws allow it, and at most one additional detached residence of up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or up to 186 m² (parcels over 40 ha), with local zoning able to be more restrictive. That frame produces farm residences — it does not produce a duplex or a sellable half duplex, and a general entitlement to any of it on a specific parcel is a parcel check, not an area claim.

The RA 4,050 m² figure is consistent with the City's SSMUH zone table, which carries RA lots at over 4,050 m²; the A-1 / Part 10 figures themselves were not re-read in Bylaw 12000 pass — not verified on the bylaw text; confirm in the current consolidated bylaw before quoting them for a listing.
